mechanics-review-d2-hard-01-01.explanation: Choose the horizontal direction towards the lower end of the incline as positive. The block stays at one point of the moving wedge, so its horizontal acceleration equals the wedge’s and vertical acceleration is zero. The smooth incline exerts only normal N in addition to weight. Its vertical component gives Ncos30°=mg. Its horizontal component gives Nsin30°=ma. Divide this by the vertical equation: a/g=tan30°. a=10tan30°=5.7735 m/s², towards the lower end.

mechanics-review-d2-hard-01-02.feedback: Correct. At F=9 N, a=0.5 m/s² and inter-block friction is 8 N.
mechanics-review-d2-hard-01-02.explanation: The top interface has a finite static-friction capacity while the floor is sliding. The floor friction is 0.100×6.00×10.0=6.00 N on the lower block. For common acceleration a, the lower block needs inter-block friction f=4a+6, with limit 0.400×2×10=8.00 N. At the limit a=0.500 m/s²; the whole system requires F=6a+6=9.00 N.

mechanics-review-d2-hard-01-03.feedback: Correct. The effective inertial denominator is 3+5+I/R²=9 kg.
mechanics-review-d2-hard-01-03.explanation: Choose 5 kg downward and 3 kg upward as positive directions with common acceleration magnitude a. For the 5 kg mass: 50−T₂=5a. For the 3 kg mass: T₁−30=3a. Pulley torque: (T₂−T₁)R=Iα; no slip gives α=a/R, hence T₂−T₁=(I/R²)a=(2/2)a. Add all three equations to cancel tensions: 20=(5+3+1)a. Thus a=20/9=2.2222 m/s²; the 5 kg mass moves downward.

mechanics-review-d2-hard-01-04.feedback: Correct. F(15)=110 N, so P=1650 W.
mechanics-review-d2-hard-01-04.explanation: At steady speed mechanical power is total resistance times speed. The two forces are 600/10=60.0 N and 3600/20=180 N. Subtracting F₀+100k=60 and F₀+400k=180 gives k=0.400 and F₀=20.0 N. At 15.0 m/s the resistance is 20.0+0.400×225=110 N, so power is 1650 W.

mechanics-review-d2-hard-01-05.feedback: Correct. At the answer, spring energy plus friction work returns 24 J; the collision has already lost 12 J.
mechanics-review-d2-hard-01-05.explanation: Momentum in the collision gives the shared speed 2(6)/3=4.0 m/s; kinetic energy after collision is 24 J. During compression this energy goes into the spring and friction: 24=50x²+6x. The positive root is x=(−6+√4836)/100=0.635414 m; the negative root is not a compression.

mechanics-review-d2-hard-01-06.feedback: Correct. 58.5/72=0.8125 of original kinetic energy remains.
mechanics-review-d2-hard-01-06.explanation: For the first collision choose the initial 12 m/s direction positive. Momentum gives 12=v₁+3v₂, and elasticity gives v₂−v₁=12. Solve: v₂=6 m/s and v₁=−6 m/s. Their kinetic energies are 54 J and 18 J. The moving 3 kg cart then sticks to the resting 1 kg cart: 3×6=4V, so V=4.5 m/s. The joined pair has energy ½×4×4.5²=40.5 J. The first cart retains its 18 J. Final/initial kinetic energy=(40.5+18)/(½×1×12²)=58.5/72=0.8125.

mechanics-review-d2-test-01-01.feedback: Correct. 2 s fall×5 m/s relative speed=10 m gain.
mechanics-review-d2-test-01-01.explanation: The package keeps drone horizontal speed while the target point continues moving. The fall time is √(2×20.0/10.0)=2.00 s. Relative horizontal speed between package and deck is 8.00−3.00=5.00 m/s. The package gains 5.00×2.00=10.0 m on that material point of the deck, so it starts 10.0 m behind it.

mechanics-review-d2-test-01-02.feedback: Correct. 3 N required divided by 10 N normal gives μ_s≥0.30.
mechanics-review-d2-test-01-02.explanation: An observed no-slip state gives a lower bound on static coefficient. Whole-system acceleration is 12.0/(1.00+3.00)=3.00 m/s². The parcel needs 1.00×3.00=3.00 N horizontal friction. Its normal force is 10.0 N, so μ_s must be at least 3.00/10.0=0.300.

mechanics-review-d2-test-01-03.feedback: Correct. Light cart 3 m/s and heavy cart 1 m/s give zero momentum and total 6 J.
mechanics-review-d2-test-01-03.explanation: Spring release creates equal opposite momenta in an isolated pair. Conserved zero momentum requires equal opposite momentum magnitudes p. Total energy is p²/(2×1)+p²/(2×3)=2p²/3=6.00 J. Thus p=3.00 kg·m/s, giving the light cart speed 3.00 m/s and the heavy cart speed 1.00 m/s.

mechanics-review-d2-test-01-04.feedback: Correct. Top contact is marginal; the compression equation includes only energy after the loop.
mechanics-review-d2-test-01-04.explanation: The bottom radial balance is N−mg=mv²/r, giving v²=40.0 and kinetic energy 4.00 J. At the top v²=40−4gr=8.0, equal to gr, so the loop is feasible; return to the bottom restores the original speed. Compression obeys 4.00=100x²+0.500x. The positive root is 0.197516 m.

mechanics-review-d2-test-01-05.feedback: Correct. Both initial reactions are positive; at the limit only the left reaction vanishes.
mechanics-review-d2-test-01-05.explanation: The left reaction initially follows from moments about x=3.00: R_left(2.5)=200(1.0)−400(0.4)=40, so R_left=16 N. Adding a force F at x=4.00 gives R_left=(40−F)/2.5. It reaches zero at F=40 N; the right reaction then carries 640 N and stays positive.

mechanics-review-d2-test-01-06.feedback: Correct. Constant resistance gives a straight v–t segment; linear drag gives falling deceleration magnitude.
